v1.feedback: The scaffold-and-collapse loop reads as a vertical constructivist tower that periodically sheds spectral afterimages — the 'eidolon' concept lands as ghost blocks drifting upward from fallen solids, which is a genuine morphological addition to the parent's stacking grammar. Two problems: (1) the mic-gated start means the piece is dead on load and silent-room energy yields near-static growth, so the form rarely fills enough frame to be compelling at default camera; consider a fallback sine-pulse so the tower always breathes. (2) The ghost shader is too faint (alpha ~0.15) and the spectral-blue palette barely differentiates ghosts from the steel solids under fog — push the ghost hue toward a cooler violet or warmer amber so the eidolon layer is instantly legible as a separate presence, not just aliasing artifacts.

v2.feedback: The eidolon concept lands — ghost doubles rising from collapsed scaffold blocks is a legible read of the word, and the amber-violet additive ghosts against cool gray solid cubes give clear spectral/material contrast. However, the mic-gate is a gallery-killer: the piece should autoplay with the synthetic pulse as default and treat mic as an optional enhancement, not the entry point. The ghost cubes are too literal — same BoxGeometry with just transparency; vertex-displacing or dissolving the ghost geometry (scale jitter, edge erosion, y-stretch as they rise) would sell 'phantom afterimage' far harder than a tinted clone. Static camera at (28,22,28) will lose the tower once it grows past ~20 rows; add a gentle orbit or adaptive lookAt that tracks the scaffold centroid.
